general: Extract every entity of the supplied types. Return exact spans from the query. Leave other text unlabelled.
S1 Nationality, people and language adjectives such as "American", "German", "British", "Swedish", "Dutch" are Other, never Country.

classes.name: ChemicalElement
classes.description: Refers to a fundamental substance characterized by its atomic number and unique properties, as found in the periodic table.
rules: CE1 Examples: "sulfur", "copper", "hydrogen", "helium", "Nihonium".

classes.name: Discipline
classes.description: Refers to a specialized field of study or research within the domains of natural science.
rules: DI1 Also label words such as biology, chemistry, astrophysics, mathematics or physics.
DI2 This also includes specific branches such as quantum chemistry.
DI3 Examples: "philosophy", "chemistry", "medicine", "electrodynamics", "spectroscopy".

classes.name: Protein
classes.description: Refers to a complex biological molecule composed of amino acids, essential for various biological functions.
rules: PR1 Examples: "Argonaute", "Histone H3", "CYP1A1", "Green fluorescent protein", "glutamate binding protein".

classes.name: Enzyme
classes.description: Refers to a specialized protein that acts as a biological catalyst, facilitating chemical reactions within organisms.
rules: EN1 If a protein is an enzyme, annotate it as an enzyme entity.
EN2 Examples: "RNA polymerase", "DNA methyltransferase", "DNA polymerase", "Spermidine synthase", "Alkaline phosphatase".

classes.name: Other
classes.description: Refers to named entities that are not included in any other category.
rules: OT1 Examples: "DNA", "Greeks", "Aryl hydrocarbon receptor repressor", "CRISPR", "Japanese".

classes.name: Scientist
classes.description: Refers to a person who is studying or has expert knowledge of one or more of the natural or physical sciences.
rules: SC1 Every person named for scientific or technical work is a Scientist, not a Person: physicists, chemists, biologists, astronomers, mathematicians, geologists, inventors, discoverers, professors, members of academies, research groups or projects.
SC2 This also holds for bare surnames and for names in lists of researchers or invitees: "Walther Bothe", "Josef Mattauch", "Mendel", "Sagan", "Thomas Edison".
SC3 A person described as a member, fellow, president or founder of an academy or scientific society is a Scientist, even by surname alone: "Libby", "Singer", "Morley", "Herschbach".
SC4 Examples: "Werner Heisenberg", "Robert Boyle", "Hans Kramers", "Isaac Newton", "Galileo Galilei".

classes.name: Award
classes.description: Refers to a recognition or distinction presented to individuals or organizations for significant contributions within the natural science domain.
rules: AW1 Fellowships are Award spans that start at "fellow": label "fellow of the Linnean Society of London", not just "Linnean Society of London".

AW2 An Award span runs to the end of its category or awarding body: "Grammy Award for Best Music Video", not just "Grammy Award"; "Rumford Medal of the British Royal Society", not just "Rumford Medal".
AW3 Examples: "Nobel Prize in Physics", "Nobel Prize in Chemistry", "Fellow of the American Physical Society", "fellow of the Royal Society", "Copley Medal of the Royal Society".

classes.name: Country
rules: CO1 Examples: "Newfoundland Colony", "France", "United States", "Russia", "Japan".

classes.name: AstronomicalObject
classes.description: Refers to a celestial entity such as a star, planet, galaxy, or nebula, present in space.
rules: AO1 A numbered minor planet keeps its catalogue number in the span: "4 Vesta", "19 Fortuna", "99942 Apophis", "51828 Ilanramon".
AO2 Examples: "Saturn", "Jupiter", "Venus", "Earth", "Uranus".

classes.name: Person
classes.description: Refers to an individual's name that is not a scientist.
rules: PE1 Person is only for people with no science role, such as actors, fictional characters, musicians, film directors, politicians, activists and outlaws: "David Tennant", "Rose Tyler", "Lil Wayne", "Gerald Ford", "Billy the Kid".
PE2 Examples: "Shenton", "Russell T Davies", "Aristotle", "Hall", "NeNe Leakes".

classes.name: ChemicalCompound
classes.description: Refers to a substance formed by combining two or more elements in fixed proportions, with distinct chemical properties.
rules: CC1 Examples: "carbon dioxide", "Adenosine triphosphate", "Nitric oxide", "ROS", "cytosine".

classes.name: Event
classes.description: Refers to a significant occurrence or happening.
rules: EV1 Such as festivals, sports events, conferences, etc.
EV2 Examples: "2017 World Championships in Athletics", "Tomorrowland", "A State Of Trance", "Ultra Music Festival", "Electric Daisy Carnival".

classes.name: Theory
classes.description: Refers to a scientifically established principle or explanation that describes natural phenomena within the scope of biology, chemistry, or astrophysics, such as orbital resonance.
rules: TH1 This encompasses laws and theories like the Ptolemaic planetary theories.
TH2 Examples: "Protein-DNA interaction", "circular dichroism", "stem cell niche theory", "Nicolaus Copernicus heliocentric theory", "metaphysics".

classes.name: University
classes.description: Refers to an educational institution of higher learning.
rules: UN1 Label organizations that are universities as 'university' entities.
UN2 Examples: "University of Sydney", "Oxford", "Uppsala University", "University of Calcutta", "Odessa University".

classes.name: Organization
classes.description: Refers to a structured group, institution, company, or association.
rules: OR1 This category covers a diverse range of organizations, including businesses, non-profits, educational institutions, and government agencies.
OR2 Hospitals, medical centers, air force bases and opera houses are Organization, not Location: "Royal Victoria Hospital", "Edwards Air Force Base", "Teatro La Fenice".
OR3 Examples: "Royal Society", "American Academy of Arts and Sciences", "National Academy of Sciences", "International Union of Geodesy and Geophysics", "American Philosophical Society".

classes.name: Location
classes.description: Refers to a specific geographical or structural location.
rules: LO1 This includes but is not limited to: places (e.g., parks, landmarks), bridges, cities, towns, villages, areas and other distinct regions.
LO2 Examples: "Cape of Good Hope", "Mumbai", "Heidelberg", "Royal Prince Alfred Hospital", "Sydney".

classes.name: AcademicJournal
classes.description: Refers to a periodical publication containing scholarly articles and research findings related to natural science disciplines.
rules: AJ1 Examples: "Angewandte Chemie", "The Astrophysical Journal", "Nature", "Chemical Reviews", "Accounts of Chemical Research".
